protocol_under_pool_pressure.why: The shipped Host StateImage pool hides a class of admission defect that only appears when StateImage capacity binds. The same fifteen checks run against the same installed bytes with the Host pool reduced to a third of the shipped size.

persistence.note: The exact f08309da packaged binary replaced its process and restored the explicitly saved 42-token control and the previously unpublished 45-token session: the latter was missing before the managed stop and available after the restart. The stop was graceful and did not force termination. This short-session gate is not a claim of loss-free shutdown for every live process session.

rollback.note: Both directions were exercised between candidate qwen38-3090-native-v0.6.2-beta.1-f08309da3cc1 and predecessor qwen38-3090-native-v0.6.0-beta.1-03f56e58ec1b, the lane's only earlier native package, which was never published: its own 2026-09-09 window failed the agent protocol phase. The candidate declares stop-event and stopped gracefully without forced termination. The predecessor predates the stop-event channel and declares terminate; its stop was a forced termination, as that mode provides. The candidate was active again afterwards. The first window, at e20060b6, failed this phase: its controller could not launch a predecessor whose packaged configuration predates context_cache.host_kv_mib, which f08309da fixes.

limitations: One active request per profile; the lane ships --max-concurrency 1 and no concurrency claim is made.

Automatic checkpoints remain best effort under live traffic. Transient refusals retry up to six times per completed turn, and admission saves a session's newest turn before evicting it, but a crash or an expired graceful wait can still leave unpublished work unsaved. The measured restart gate proves the two short target sessions survived, not globally loss-free shutdown.

Save-before-evict with ceiling-class sessions was exercised on the RTX 5090 only (releases/v0.8.7/qualification/rtx5090.json, docs/measurements/2026-09-24-durable-session-eviction.json, docs/measurements/2026-09-24-publication-barrier.json). This lane's window runs its own phases and did not construct a ceiling-class eviction. Quota reclamation order, compaction handoffs and the planner's budget fallback were measured on the RTX 4090 with a supervised server running that lane's configuration (docs/measurements/2026-09-29-long-session-cache.json), not on this card.

Restore may reclaim a resident session only when its latest checkpoint is reproducible. Restore and response-store capacity refusal remain possible. The lane pins an 8192 MiB host-KV pool with 24 host-state slots and declares no host-memory floor; it was qualified on one host, and no smaller-host profile is qualified.

A managed start could fail when the driver refused to pin the host-KV pool (alphastorm/omp-ninfer#48). Since b0e8c2fa the runtime commits and releases each pinned allocation's size plus 1/64 first; every managed start in this window pinned the 8192 MiB pool, and a recurrence reports the commit limit, available commit and available memory.

A managed start refuses while any process holds 1 GiB or more of dedicated GPU memory, the desktop compositor included. Before this window, with the qualification host's desktop session signed in and its applications closed, the compositor alone held about 1,070 MiB; the window ran with the console signed out, the compositor at about 290 MiB.

While the lane serves, the GPU-owner controller holds the card at the qualified 300 W power limit inside a 301 W envelope and restores the owner's 370 W limit on stop; the C1 benchmark peaked at 299.92 W. GPU keep-warm is off (engine.gpu_keep_warm_ms 0); keep-warm was measured on the RTX 4090 only (docs/measurements/2026-09-27-rtx4090-keep-warm-long-spin.json).

The C1 benchmark fixture (28,000 characters of one repeated sentence) is trajectory-sensitive: its acceptance and decode rate move with changes in prefill summation order or fixture length (docs/measurements/2026-09-13-rtx4090-c1-fixture-sensitivity.json). This is the lane's first passing native window, so its 102.64 tok/s at 93.43% acceptance has no like-for-like predecessor.

Rollback was proven against the lane's unpublished v0.6.0-beta.1 native package, not a published one. The separate v0.2 durable lineage installed on the host was not running, was stopped for the window and left untouched.
The OMP phase ran the unmodified upstream Oh My Pi 18.4.0 Windows client from a fresh client root on the target.
Measured numbers apply only to this package, this machine, and this profile.
